description: Measured on develop e515ae314 (AOT), distiller-shaped decode over the first 16,000 lines of a compile log, records retained: 1,195 collections copy 7.5 GB while live data peaks at 25 MB; the same decode with nothing retained copies 26 MB and runs in 7.8 s instead of 15.0 s. Heap::collect is a full Cheney copy, so every retained record is recopied by every collection, and procbin::mso_unreached_closures / mso_sweep walk the chain of every live ProcBin each time (18% of a 32,000-line profile). Because a collection is due only after allocating as much as is live (Heap::should_gc), the copying is bounded by total allocation: it is a constant factor (about 2x here), not a scaling defect. The first lever is allocating less (fz-sc8.183); re-measure this after it lands. Goal if still material: survivors are not recopied by every collection (generations, as BEAM), and the off-heap chain walk is proportional to what the collection examined. Needs a proposal page. Data: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/slow (rt*.jsonl, samp.txt).
title: A collection copies only what is new, and walks no chain of every live binary
